newsitem.title: INDIA: India worst emerging market performer in Nov MSCI.
newsitem.headline: India worst emerging market performer in Nov MSCI.

text.p: India was the weakest performer in the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) index for emerging markets during November, an MSCI statement said on Tuesday.
Emerging markets which fared poorly during the month included India (-8.9 percent), Chile (-6.3 percent) and South Africa (-5.6 percent).
"Overall, 19 of the emerging market countries followed by MSCI showed gains during the month, while only eight registered declines," MSCI said.

"The EMF (emerging markets free) index was held to a relatively modest gain of 1.6 percent because the decliners included some of the larger countries in the index, such as India and South Africa as well as Korea (-1.8 percent)."
Strongest performers among emerging markets during November were China (+11.5 percent), Indonesia (8.8 percent) and Argentina (6.7 percent).

"In China, the outlook for economic growth attracted capital from both domestic and international investors. In Indonesia investors responded to the outlook for lower inflation and the adoption earlier this year of more flexible exchange rate policies," MSCI said.
Venezuela at +116.1 percent is the strongest performer among emerging markets in the year-to-date, it said.
"The market has been helped by strong revenues flowing from the country's oil producers and investor confidence over a series of government economic reforms," MSCI said.
Weakest MSCI performers this year among emerging markets have been Thailand (-29.8 percent) and Korea (-29.4 percent).
"Both countries have been hurt by slowing economic growth and political turmoil," the statement said.
MSCI said low interest rates in the U.S. helped fuel a worldwide stock market rally in November, with all 22 developed markets followed by MSCI showing a gain during the month.
The MSCI World index of 22 developed markets climbed 5.5 percent during the month.
Strongest developed markets in November were Finland (8.2 percent), Spain (8.2 percent) and Hong Kong (7.9 percent).
"In Hong Kong, optimism about the Chinese economy and the outlook for lower interest rates, which are linked to U.S. rates, boosted stocks in the important property sector," MSCI said.
Worst performers among developed markets during November were Switzerland (0.8 percent), New Zealand (1.1 percent) and Japan (1.9 percent).
The strongest performing developed markets in the year-to-date are Sweden (+34.4 percent), Canada (+31.0 percent) and Hong Kong (+29.9 percent).
